title: fix: decode UTF-8 in computer shell command substitution
author: Drjacky

gist.summary: Fixed UTF-8 decoding in the computer-mcp bash tool’s `$(...)` command substitution on both normal and `exit`/`return` paths. Captured `Época` now measures 6 bytes rather than 8 when used in a later command; plain text and invalid UTF-8 remain unchanged. Bumped the shell loader revision from `bytes-read` to `bytes-substitution` so cached isolates load the patch, which fails at startup if it no longer applies. Documented bundled jq limitations and workarounds: use `env.NAME` instead of `--arg`/`--argjson`/`--rawfile`, `[(]` instead of `\(` in regexes, and `def f(a): a as $a | ...` instead of `def f($a)`. Added tests for substitution through byte output, jq, pipes, base64 decoding, functions, exit status, and strings passed to jq.
